anomalies.observed: In the WATER LEVEL SENSOR/SWITCHES block, R6 (10 kΩ) is tied as a pull-up on the FLOAT_HIGH line and R9 is a 10 MΩ pulldown on the FLOAT_LOW line. The specification states the opposite biasing and a 10 kΩ value: 'R6 FLOAT_LOW +3V3 10k, R9 GND FLOAT_HIGH 10k'.
anomalies.expected: Per the spec, FLOAT_LOW should carry the 10 kΩ pull-up (R6) and FLOAT_HIGH a 10 kΩ pulldown (R9). A 10 MΩ pulldown is three orders of magnitude off and, combined with the pull-up/pulldown swap, leaves the float-switch inputs weakly defined.

anomalies.impact: The water-level float interlocks (low-level pump cutoff and high-level overflow stop, which also gate the pump/valve bases via R2/R11) become noise-sensitive and possibly inverted, undermining the ATO/pump safety logic.

anomalies.observed: The TF-Luna LiDAR (PR1) is wired through header H1 to +5V, GND, I2C_SDA and I2C_SCL in the 'Water Height Sensor' block.
anomalies.expected: The specification documents PR1 as excluded from the board and unwired: 'its pins are "free" and it is marked on_board: no / excluded from the board; it is not wired into any net', and water level is intended to be sensed by an ultrasonic sensor/floats, not the LiDAR.

anomalies.observed: The ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch is implemented with T5 (AO3400A, a 30 V small-signal N-MOSFET), while T3 (AON6407) is instead used as the series MOSFET in the 24 V input reverse-polarity block.
anomalies.expected: The specification assigns the ATO valve to the AON6407: 'T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch ... drives ATO_VALVE net'. Switching a 24 V inductive solenoid with a 30 V-rated AO3400A leaves almost no margin for flyback transients.
